title: Prefetch policy safeguard and phased adoption playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary: Design and implement a conservative, automatable playbook for rolling out prefix/KV prefetch and TTL changes that maximizes cost savings while bounding customer-visible regressions. This ticket covers hit-rate forecasting, sample-based policy tuning, deterministic canary orchestration, and an automated safe-apply/rollback controller for config changes (prefetch thresholds, per-prefix TTL laddering, and cachekey harmonization).

Context: We have multiple initiatives that show 10–35% token-cost reductions from smarter prefix caching and prefetching, but historical rollouts produced outlier customer regressions (rare high-miss prefixes and latency spikes under heavy tail). The goal is an operationally simple, auditable flow that: 1) produces reliable hit-rate forecasts for candidate policy changes, 2) recommends conservative per-prefix TTL/prefetch values, 3) dry-runs changes under shadow traffic and offline simulators, and 4) executes safe staged rollouts with automated rollback triggers.

Goals/Success metrics (quantified):
- Net cost reduction: target 8–12% on token spend for qualifying workloads within 30 days.
- Quality guardrails: p95 latency delta <= +5% and end-to-end error rate delta <= +0.05% during rollout.
- Miss-rate uplift cap: per-prefix miss_rate_delta <= +3% (hard cap).
- Safety: automated rollback triggers that execute without manual intervention when thresholds are exceeded.

Approach/Phases:
1) Offline sampling and hit forecasting (owner: Data & Runtime): build a sampling pipeline that computes per-prefix and per-affix hit curves using stratified sampling across regions, model types, and sequence lengths. Use a lightweight GLM + monotonic smoothing (hit_rate ~ log(prefetch_size) + prefix_freq + seq_len_quantile) to produce conservative mean+CI forecasts.
2) Policy generator (owner: Runtime): convert forecasts to a set of candidate policies (TTL ladders, prefetch size, eligibility filters). Prioritize conservative candidates that reduce cost while keeping the upper-bound of predicted miss rate under the cap.
3) Shadow validation and synthetic load (owner: SRE): run candidates in shadow against live traffic for 48h and against synthetic heavy-tail replay for 2h to expose worst-case prefixes. Collect token-level cost savings, miss-rate per prefix, tail latencies, and KV load.
4) Staged rollout controller (owner: Platform): implement an orchestration flow: dry-run -> 1% traffic for 2h -> 10% for 6h -> 50% for 24h -> 100% gradual. Each stage has automated checks (miss-rate, p95 latency, errors, KV QPS). If any check crosses thresholds, controller triggers circuit-breaker rollback for affected shards/prefix groups.
5) Post-rollout autotuner (owner: Autotune): gather real-world signals and propose further per-prefix adjustments; proposals pass back through the shadow validation flow before applying.

Automation & Safety mechanisms:
- Tiered CI: every policy change is produced as a YAML diff in PR pipeline with reproducible input snapshot (sampled traffic window) and offline-simulator results attached.
- Shadow-only metric buckets and golden signal comparisons (Grafana dashboard UID: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-prefetch-sim).
- Rollback policy: circuit-breaker with soft and hard thresholds (soft: warn + throttle; hard: immediate rollback).
- Scoped rollouts: group prefixes by volatility score (entropy + recent miss spike) and do not allow aggressive TTL reduction on top volatile groups.

Data needs & instrumentation:
- 14-day sliding window of per-prefix counts, hits, misses, average token cost, and p95/p99 latency; store aggregated snapshots for reproducibility.
- Lightweight provenance tags on requests to map inference requests -> prefix keying rules for audit.
- Notebook & sim artifacts: drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-prefetch-sim-artifacts, and notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/notebooks/prefetch-sim.ipynb.

Acceptance criteria (for Merging policy-generator):
- Forecast model produces calibrated CI that contains observed miss rate <= 90% of the time in post-hoc checks.
- Shadow 48h run demonstrates no prefix exceeding miss_rate_delta cap in production traffic sampling.
- Rollout controller integrates with existing canary infra and can perform an automated rollback without manual operator CLI.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Conservative defaults vs. missed savings: We bias toward conservative TTL reduction in the first wave; might leave 2–4% upside on the table until the autotuner proves stable.
- Prefetch cost vs. latency: aggressive prefetch reduces misses but increases KV traffic; we plan to use cost-per-miss avoided as an objective to pick candidates.
- Label drift: prefix semantics can change (new product features). We will require a quarterly recompute of volatility/affinity scores.

Deliverables:
- policy-generator service (runtime repo PR) + CI artifacts,
- shadow validation harness and synthetic replay job,
- rollout controller changes + circuit-breaker implementation,
- Grafana dashboards and a short runbook for on-call.

Links (live artifacts & PRs):
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Prefetch+Policy+Safeguard
- Simulation notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/notebooks/prefetch-sim.ipynb
- Runtime PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
- Platform rollout controller draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/678
- Shadow dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-prefetch-sim

Timeline & next milestones:
- 2026-03-05: sampling pipeline prototype complete (done)
- 2026-03-12: initial policy-generator prototype + simulation results (this ticket updated)
- 2026-03-20: shadow validation integration and 48h run start
- 2026-03-28: staged rollout controller wired to platform canary infra
- 2026-03-31: target to reach 10% traffic production cohort if safe

Operational notes for on-call:
- Immediate mitigation steps in runbook: disable prefetch ruleset -> redirect to conservative fallback TTL set -> notify runtime SRE on-call.

Longer-term: integrate this playbook into the KV Adviser UI as a "Suggest & Apply" flow so Solutions Engineers can preview cost/latency trade-offs for a customer and request staging via the console.
